codeReview.summary: The k8s-status-monitor feature implementation is complete and well-structured. It provides comprehensive Job status monitoring with polling, state detection, event capture, and OOM detection. The code follows Go conventions and includes extensive unit tests covering state detection, OOM detection, and event storage.

issues.description: Error from Redis cache.SetStatus in handleStateChange is logged but not returned - this is acceptable for fire-and-forget status updates but could lead to silent failures if Redis is down

handleJobNotFound updates status to 'cancelled' but validation contract VAL-CROSS-004 indicates cancellation should preserve partial results. The current implementation doesn't check for or preserve partial results before marking cancelled.
updateProgress calls evalRepo.UpdateStatus even when progress hasn't changed - this could cause unnecessary database writes. Consider checking if progress changed before updating.
The GetEvents method uses 'source LIKE k8s-%' pattern but this could miss events if source doesn't match exactly. Consider making the filtering more explicit.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker created new package internal/k8s/monitor/ following the established k8s package structure pattern (k8s/job/, k8s/configmap/, k8s/secret/). This follows existing conventions.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: internal/k8s/monitor/ follows same pattern as internal/k8s/job/creator.go

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker used interface-based design for EventStore (InMemoryEventStore, DBLogStore) which follows repository pattern from AGENTS.md
sharedStateObservations.evidence: EventStore interface with NewInMemoryEventStore() and NewDBLogStore() constructors

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker followed backend-worker skill procedure correctly - created unit tests, ran go build/vet/fmt, verified tests pass. skillFeedback confirms followedProcedure: true with no deviations.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff shows all verification commands passed (go build, go vet, go fmt, go test with 26 test cases)

sharedStateObservations.observation: No new services were started by the worker - the feature only requires Kubernetes client-go which is configured via existing kubectl context. No services.yaml updates needed.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript shows no additional service starts beyond existing k8s context

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker correctly used client-go fake client for testing (fake.NewSimpleClientset()) which is appropriate for unit testing without real K8s cluster. This pattern could be documented in library.

VAL-K8S-013.description: Job Status Correctly Reflects Running State
VAL-K8S-013.evidence: detectJobState() returns 'running' when JobHasActive() is true (line 168), handleStateChange() updates status to StatusRunning with progress 50

VAL-K8S-014.description: Job Status Correctly Reflects Completed State
VAL-K8S-014.evidence: detectJobState() returns 'completed' when JobIsCompleted() is true (line 165), handleStateChange() updates to StatusCompleted with progress 100, stops monitoring

VAL-K8S-015.evidence: JobEvent types defined (Created, Started, Completed, Failed, Deleted, OOMKilled), EventStore interface with StoreEvent/GetEvents, InMemoryEventStore and DBLogStore implementations, events recorded in handleStateChange() and checkForOOMKilled()

VAL-K8S-016.evidence: creator.go sets BackoffLimit to 3 (int32Ptr(3)), detectJobState() returns 'failed' when JobIsFailed() is true, handleStateChange() handles failed state

VAL-K8S-017.description: OOM Killed Pods Detected and Reported
VAL-K8S-017.evidence: IsOOMKilled() checks exit code 137 and OOMKilled reason in both containers and init containers, checkForOOMKilled() detects OOM and records EventPodOOMKilled event, marks evaluation as failed when OOM detected

summary: The k8s-status-monitor feature is well-implemented with comprehensive test coverage (26+ test cases). All VAL-K8S-013 through VAL-K8S-017 assertions are covered. The implementation includes Job status polling, state detection (Running/Completed/Failed), event capture with both in-memory and DB storage, and OOM killed pod detection via exit code 137 or OOMKilled reason. Code quality is good with proper error handling and interface-based design following project conventions.
